record.title: Allowed telemetry strings may cause superlinear synchronous redaction before truncation
record.description: A producer holding a service-bound plugin Credential can submit a valid Sentry event with a long alphabetic event.type below the one-MiB envelope limit. The mapper redacts that entire string before truncating its normalized type to 128 characters, and its payload projection can omit the original top-level type. The shared email detector has an unanchored greedy local-part expression that can repeatedly scan suffixes of a non-matching token. This creates a source-grounded candidate from one Project's telemetry capability to CPU work on the shared API process; the final Event can be small enough for the broker cap. Plugin payload and identity processing reach the same detector under the smaller plugin request cap. No timing, service interruption, or cross-Project delay was demonstrated, and no severity is assigned.
record.claimed_root_cause: The shared redactor applies an unanchored, potentially quadratic email regex synchronously to caller-controlled strings without a per-string work budget. Sentry eventType invokes it before the only type-length truncation. The strongest visible controls are the one-MiB Sentry raw/parser caps, the plugin default 65,536-byte and maximum 102,400-byte cap, client request throttling, four redaction passes, and a downstream 128-KiB stream message limit. They bound request count, total bytes, passes, or final publication size, but do not establish linear regex work or preempt a synchronous call. Whether the supported Bun engine optimizes this pattern enough to prevent meaningful shared impact is unresolved.

trace.description: A throttled caller with a valid plugin publish Credential submits an envelope; Project and service remain constrained by SentryKeyGuard.
The route accepts a raw envelope up to one MiB; it does not impose a separate maximum on the JSON event.type string.
The parser checks whole-envelope and event-item byte caps and parses an event JSON object without a per-field string-length bound.
The accepted event object is passed to mapSentryEvent before final envelope validation or broker publication.
The raw exception type or event.type is passed to redact in full at line 25; the 128-character slice occurs afterward at line 28. A long top-level event.type is not copied into the mapped payload.
The synchronous detector loop calls String.replace for the email expression on the API request's execution path; the maximum of four passes does not limit the work of one match attempt.

The unanchored [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+ local part followed by a required @ can rescan successive suffixes of a long non-matching alphabetic token. Engine behavior and meaningful shared CPU delay require bounded validation.

evidence.description: eventType chooses unbounded event text, redacts before truncation, then emits at most 128 normalized suffix characters; the mapped payload at lines 87-91 contains only exception, message, and request.
The email pattern is /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g, with no preceding token boundary or explicit local-part length bound.
redact invokes detector passes synchronously and has no cancellation, worker isolation, or elapsed-work budget.
The Sentry raw-body limit is one MiB; this is an effective input-byte control but permits a long single type token.
The parser independently enforces the default whole-envelope and event-item byte limits before event mapping; the candidate must remain within both.
Both ingestion controllers use the configured client throttler. A meaningful proof must use a single admitted request, rather than rely on bypassing or exceeding the rate limit.
Plugin events have a 65,536-byte default and 102,400-byte configuration ceiling; the adjacent throttler defaults to 60 requests per 60,000 ms.
The plugin sibling reaches redact through recursive payload cleaning; privacy.ts also applies the same detector set to metadata using hasSensitiveText.
The declared 128-KiB stream message limit is downstream of the Sentry type redaction and can still admit the mapper's small final representation.
The API bootstrap starts one Nest application listener. The reviewed redaction path executes in that application, without a source-visible per-Project worker boundary.

blockers: Complete OS-enforced memory and cumulative-disk sandbox controls are not established, and the assignment forbids all target-controlled execution. No regex fixture, API process, test, or benchmark was run; there is no observed result or retained local artifact.

The supported Bun/JavaScriptCore regex optimizer or fallback behavior may change the cost of this pattern. A safe bounded local check must establish growth within the accepted body sizes and a meaningful delay to unrelated work on the same isolated API process before calling this an availability vulnerability.

validation_plan.local: After the parent establishes all required OS-enforced sandbox controls, use an empty allowlisted environment, no external networking, read-only source/tools, scratch-only writes, low CPU/memory/process/file/disk limits, and a short hard wall-clock deadline. First compare one call to the exact redactor on non-matching ASCII alphabetic strings at small increasing sizes such as 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 bytes, stopping on the first decisive result or deadline. Then, only if the cost warrants it, use an isolated in-memory Sentry controller/service fixture with a dummy verified plugin Credential, fake publisher, header event_id of 32 lowercase hex characters, and an event JSON object containing timestamp: 1, level: info, and type set to the same bounded alphabetic string. Confirm acceptance below the one-MiB caps, observe an independent timer or dummy second-Project request on that same process, and stop at the minimum measurable shared delay. Exercise the plugin sibling separately below its configured byte cap. If the engine remains effectively linear or prevents meaningful shared delay, reject the candidate. Do not send traffic to a deployed API, broker, or provider.
